title: OpenAI will buy Pierre Computer to fold Code Storage into Codex, aiming at the GitHub layer where agents ship code
summary: OpenAI announced on November 4 that it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc., the startup behind Code Storage and open-source tools already used inside the Codex app for browsing files and reviewing changes. Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries power those surfaces today, and OpenAI said that once the deal closes it wants to bring Code Storage into Codex so developers and coding agents can move from the first branch an agent creates to deployment in one place. Financial terms were not disclosed; Pierre’s open-source projects will stay open source, and customers can keep using Code Storage after closing while OpenAI works the features into Codex. Axios reported the move as OpenAI joining rivals challenging Microsoft’s GitHub as AI agents write more of the world’s software. The closing still needs customary conditions, including regulatory approvals, and until then the two companies remain separate.

title: S&P 500 futures edge higher while Nasdaq slips as chip and data-center names stay under pressure
summary: U.S. stock index futures were mixed early Thursday after Wednesday’s midterm-driven rally, Reuters reported. At 7:04 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 330 points, or 0.62%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 15.5 points, or 0.2%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 145.5 points, or 0.51%. Semiconductor and AI infrastructure names remained soft: Nvidia was down about 0.8% premarket, Marvell Technology off 3.4%, and Intel slipping 2%, while data-center operators IREN, Hut 8, and Applied Digital fell between 1.1% and 2.7%, and CoreWeave and Nebius each fell about 3%. Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Alphabet were up more than 1% as some investors treated a slower AI buildout as a relief for large-cap tech. UBS strategists warned that data-center pauses could put roughly 30% of expected 2028 capacity additions at risk.

title: Qualcomm tops the quarter but guides light, and handset chip sales fall 26% as memory costs bite
summary: Qualcomm reported fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.17 a share on adjusted revenue of $10.44 billion, beating LSEG estimates of $2.16, CNBC reported, but its current-quarter outlook trailed Wall Street and the stock slid about 7% after hours, then about 9.6% in Thursday premarket trading per Reuters. Handset chip sales fell 26% to $5.14 billion, below a StreetAccount estimate of $5.21 billion, as rising memory costs pushed handset makers to raise prices. Automotive revenue jumped 89% to $1.99 billion, and CEO Cristiano Amon said data-center revenue was $650 million in the quarter with a $5 billion target for fiscal 2027. “We don’t have a demand issue; it’s a supply issue,” Amon said of the data-center push. For the current quarter, Qualcomm guided adjusted EPS of $2.15 to $2.35 on revenue of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, versus analyst expectations of $2.27 and about $10.48 billion.

title: Nvidia and AI infrastructure names slip further as investors price in slower data-center buildouts
summary: Chip stocks extended Wednesday’s losses into Thursday’s premarket session as investors weighed Democratic wins in key data-center states, Reuters reported. Nvidia was down about 0.8%, Marvell Technology off 3.4%, and Intel down 2%, while AI server maker Dell fell 2.9% and utilities tied to the power buildout, including GE Vernova and Constellation Energy, also traded lower. Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius Group each fell about 3%. UBS strategists said pauses on data centers could slow the buildout into 2028, with roughly 30% of expected 2028 additions at risk, though they also argued much of that risk is already reflected in semiconductor valuations near multi-year lows. Large-cap platforms Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet rose more than 1% on the view that a slower infrastructure race could ease spending pressure.

title: TeraWulf lands a Google credit backstop for its $19 billion Anthropic leases in Kentucky
summary: TeraWulf said on November 4 that it signed credit support agreements with Google LLC covering debt financing behind roughly $19 billion of contracted lease commitments with Anthropic at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky. The 20-year leases cover about 401 megawatts of critical IT load across three buildings, with phased ready-for-service dates expected from late 2027 through the second quarter of 2028. Alphabet’s senior unsecured debt is rated AA+ by S&P and Aa2 by Moody’s, which TeraWulf said strengthens its path to competitive project financing. The company also signed a definitive EPC agreement with Fluor for three data center buildings on a guaranteed-maximum-price basis. Google’s backstop becomes effective as each lease’s final data hall commences; if Anthropic defaults, Google can assume the lease or, in some cases, pay a termination fee and take equity in the project company.

title: Google agrees to backstop Anthropic’s Kentucky data-center leases as TeraWulf locks in Fluor for the build
summary: Data-center operator TeraWulf disclosed on November 4 that Google signed three credit support agreements tied to Anthropic’s long-term leases at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, covering about $19 billion in contracted rent over the initial term. Anthropic’s obligation to pay rent starts as each data hall is delivered across three buildings totaling roughly 401 MW of critical IT capacity. TeraWulf also moved Fluor from early engineering into a full EPC role with defined milestones and open-book cost reporting. In an SEC filing, TeraWulf said that if Anthropic misses rent or becomes insolvent, Google can pay overdue rent and assume the lease, or under certain conditions pay a termination fee and receive equity in Raylan Data LLC. Delivery is expected to begin in late 2027 and finish in the second quarter of 2028.

title: Menlo Ventures says enterprise AI spend hit $177 billion, up 5.4× in a year as agents take over the tokens
summary: Menlo Ventures’ fourth annual State of Enterprise AI report, published November 3, estimates U.S. enterprise AI deployment spending reached about $176.8 billion by September 2026, up from $33 billion a year earlier. The firm says agents now generate 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, roughly seven times human-driven usage, and that frontier labs capture 69% of deployment dollars. Anthropic’s share of enterprise LLM API spend rose to 55% and OpenAI’s to 31%, while Google’s fell to 9%. Coding apps account for $34 billion of a $77.3 billion application market, and Menlo estimates every dollar spent building models is generating about $1.70 of deployment revenue. The figures are annualized run-rate estimates drawn from a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 enterprise decision-makers plus public filings, not a sum of invoices.

title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds native GIFs and SVG export, and OpenAI says users now make 4 billion images a week
summary: OpenAI released Images 2.6 on November 4 across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, saying image generation is about 50% faster and that people now create 4 billion images a week, up from 3 billion in September. ChatGPT can generate animated GIFs from a prompt or an uploaded photo, then let users change playback speed and edit individual frames, The Verge reported. Developers get GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for fast low-quality images in as little as six seconds and Sunburst for higher-fidelity work with stronger edit consistency, plus SVG export and image markup in the API. The update is available globally on all ChatGPT and Codex subscription tiers on web, desktop, and mobile.

title: Together AI launches Together Compiler, letting agent swarms retune open-model inference as traffic shifts
summary: Together AI said on November 4 that many of the models on its endpoints are now optimized by AI agents through Together Compiler, which it calls a production-scale recursive self-improvement loop for open-source inference. The system treats performance tuning as an agentic search problem: agents explore optimization patterns against a persistent engine that can hot-reload candidate forward passes as models, traffic shapes, and chips change. Together notes that 80% of OpenRouter traffic already hits models released in the last three months, so static hand-tuned configs age quickly. Continuous Compilation is live on selected serverless endpoints, with limited beta access for customers who want it on dedicated deployments.

title: OpenAI’s cyber pipeline finds and patches 948 Linux root paths in one run at a $1.2 million API cost
summary: OpenAI published “A thousand fewer paths to root” on November 4, describing an autonomous pipeline that, in a mid-October run with an upcoming cyber model, dynamically reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and produced 948 unique local privilege-escalation exploits plus candidate patches. The end-to-end run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, or about $1,279 per LPE. Human researchers review outputs before reporting; OpenAI said it has already sent hundreds of critical reports and patches and is working with Patch the Planet partners on the rest. The agents also used at least 10 novel exploitation techniques in a sampled set of exploits, according to OpenAI. The company frames the work as raising attackers’ costs and helping maintainers keep pace as model capability grows.

title: Fal doubles its valuation to $16 billion after a $1.3 billion Series F led by Bessemer
summary: Fal, the San Francisco startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, raised $1.3 billion in a Series F led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price participating, TechCrunch reported on November 3 citing Bloomberg. The round values Fal at $16 billion, double the $8 billion valuation from April. Fal said it announced Series E and F together for a combined $1.65 billion raised across both rounds, with Sequoia leading the earlier one. Bloomberg reported that Fal had surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year as demand for open-source model inference surged. Co-founders Burkay Gur and Gorkem Yurtseven started the company in 2021.

title: A Bangladeshi CSE student builds Axiom so classmates can use ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini without shared logins
summary: Akhlak Hossain Jim, a final-year computer science student at East West University in Dhaka, built Axiom with two co-founders after watching classmates buy shared AI logins on Facebook and Telegram, The Business Standard Graduates reported on November 3. Shared accounts expose chat history and can vanish without warning, while global subscriptions priced around $20 a month are hard to pay for without a foreign card and poorly matched to bursty exam-week usage. Axiom gives students a private workspace that reaches major models through one account, bills in taka for what they use, and supports bKash, with credits starting from as low as Tk50 and lasting about a year. The project is bootstrapped from Jim’s freelance income; he says success means a Bangladeshi undergrad reaching the same class of tools as a student at MIT without a shared login or a favor from a senior.

title: A Queen’s Belfast medical student built Virtual Medic so classmates can rehearse OSCEs with AI patients
summary: Abhay Shivamurthy, a 22-year-old medical student at Queen’s University Belfast, created Virtual Medic so students can practice clinical consultations with animated AI patients that talk back and score what was covered or missed, FE News reported ahead of the November 13 ESBF Champion of Champions final in London. He started building the night he finished his own second-year practical exams after finding that rehearsing with friends felt artificial. Universities can author their own cases and track progress in an OSCE-style format. Virtual Medic is one of the AI-powered finalists competing for a share of a £16,500 prize fund at the Royal Academy of Engineering.

title: A Southampton student designs ISARS, an AI gadget that hears malaria mosquitoes by their wingbeat
summary: Ulrich Ronald Mefenya Tanetsing, a 23-year-old biomedical engineering postgraduate at the University of Southampton who grew up in Cameroon, built ISARS, a low-cost device that uses wingbeat sound to spot malaria-carrying mosquito species and then emits adapting acoustic signals to disrupt their navigation, FE News reported. The system is designed to work without chemicals, internet, or heavy infrastructure so it can sit in homes in remote communities. Ulrich said the idea clicked after a documentary about submarines using sound to steer whales, and he is taking ISARS to the ESBF Champion of Champions final in London on November 13.

title: Moncus Park hosts An Evening Under the Oaks tonight, its 2026 gala under the live oaks
summary: Moncus Park’s 2026 gala, An Evening Under the Oaks presented by First Horizon Bank, runs tonight, Thursday, November 5, from 6:00 to 9:30 p.m. Guests get a cocktail hour and gourmet dinner that support the park’s operations and maintenance. Regular park parking is $2 an hour Tuesday through Sunday, with rates that can vary for special events. The gala sits on a busy park week that also includes Friday’s Food Truck Friday Fall Edition and Saturday’s farmers market.

title: Food Truck Friday’s Fall Edition rolls back into Moncus Park tomorrow from 11 to 2
summary: Moncus Park’s Food Truck Friday: Fall Edition returns Friday, November 6, from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., with local food trucks, shade under the oaks, tables inside or out, fans, and yard games. The limited October–November run brings lunch crowds to the park on Fridays before the Saturday Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market. Parking at Moncus Park is $2 an hour Tuesday through Sunday.

title: Downtown Alive! brings The Pine Leaf Boys to Parc Sans Souci on Friday night, free
summary: Downtown Alive!, Acadiana’s free outdoor concert series, features The Pine Leaf Boys on Friday, November 6, from 6:00 to 8:30 p.m. at Parc Sans Souci, 201 E. Vermilion Street, with opening act The Josh Mendoza Experience. The Children’s Museum of Acadiana will have CMA on the Go! STEM activities for kids, and an after-party follows at High Notes at Chez La Fête with Lost Bayou Ramblers. Organizers ask guests to leave ice chests at home and support the beverage tent and downtown food vendors. Metered downtown parking is free after 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

title: The Lafayette Nutcracker Market fills the Cajundome Convention Center on Saturday
summary: The Lafayette Nutcracker Market opens Saturday, November 7, at 10:00 a.m. at the Cajundome Convention Center, 444 Cajundome Blvd., with boutique clothing, holiday and home décor, gourmet food, and handmade jewelry. Tickets are sold day-of at the box office; online Ticketmaster purchases add fees. Teachers, military, and first responders get complimentary admission with ID, and guests under 15 are free. The venue enforces a clear-bag policy.

title: The Ragin’ Cajuns host South Alabama at Cajun Field on Saturday afternoon
summary: Louisiana’s Ragin’ Cajuns play South Alabama in Lafayette on Saturday, November 7, at 4:00 p.m. CT on ESPN+, according to the team’s 2026 football schedule. The home Sun Belt matchup is the next game on the slate before Louisiana travels to ULM on November 12 for an in-state rivalry night on ESPN2. Kickoff details and ticketing remain on the Ragin’ Cajuns athletics site.

title: Moncus Park hosts the Tunnel to Towers 5K on Sunday morning
summary: The Tunnel to Towers 5K Run & Walk returns to Moncus Park on Sunday, November 8, from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m., honoring FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller and supporting first responders and military families. The 3.1-mile course is open to runners and walkers; this is the fourth Acadiana year for the event. Registration details are linked from the Moncus Park calendar and RunSignup.
